title: It Compiled, and the Answer Is Wrong

questions.question: A calculation returns a number that is exactly half what it should be. What is the most useful next thought?
options: Something was averaged, or applied twice, so look for the factor rather than reading the whole function
The compiler optimised it incorrectly
A rounding error accumulated
The input was wrong
questions.explanation: A wrong number is wrong in a way, and the way is a short list. Turning it wrong into out by a factor of two is a hypothesis, and a hypothesis can be tested in a minute.

questions.question: Both wheels turn at the same speed and the heading changes. What does that tell you before you read any code?
options: The turn rate is wrong, and the geometry of the position update is not the suspect
The tolerance is too small
The simulation ran for too long
Nothing, since the heading may legitimately drift
questions.explanation: It cannot change, by the definition of the model. Each property that holds removes a region of the code from suspicion, which is most of the search done without reading a line.

questions.question: Five hundred steps give a wrong answer. What is worth checking first?
options: One step, since correct at one and wrong at five hundred means the error accumulates rather than being in the geometry
Whether the loop count is right
The last step, since that is where the answer appears
Every step, printed to a file
questions.explanation: Halve the input, not the code. The smallest input that still fails is the cheapest thing you will ever debug, and if one step is already wrong you can compute the right answer by hand.

questions.question: A heading of 3.14159 and one of -3.14159 are compared by subtraction. What happens?
options: The difference reads as a full turn, so two identical directions are reported as different
The comparison is correct, since the numbers differ
The result is not a number
The sign is lost
questions.explanation: A false report of a bug is worse than a missed one, because you go looking for something that is not there. Take the difference through atan2 of its sine and cosine, which throws the whole turns away.

questions.question: Why do the tests in this lesson feed the checks trajectories that are deliberately wrong?
options: A check that cannot fail is not a check, and one that always returns true passes every test built from correct data
To measure how fast the checks run
To show what a wrong trajectory looks like
Because the correct trajectories were not available
questions.explanation: Three of the traps in this lesson were confirmed by writing the bug into the reference, and one of them is caught only by these tests.

questions.question: You decide to print values. Where do you print first?
options: At the boundary, the inputs and the result, since half the time the input was already wrong
In the middle of the calculation, where the bug is
Everywhere, then read it afterwards
Only on the step that fails
questions.explanation: And print the value you are not suspicious of, because that is where it will be.
